name: 40 CFR 122.41(l)(4), (l)(6), (l)(7), (m), (n): NPDES standard conditions (DMRs, 24-hour and 5-day noncompliance reporting, bypass, upset)

license: US federal statute/regulation text: not subject to copyright (17 U.S.C. 105); public domain.
legal_basis: 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6)(i): "The permittee shall report any noncompliance which may endanger health or the environment. Any information shall be provided orally within 24 hours from the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances. A report shall also be provided within 5 days of the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances." … "For noncompliance events related to combined sewer overflows, sanitary sewer overflows, or bypass events, these reports must include ... the type of event ..., type of sewer overflow structure ..., discharge volumes untreated by the treatment works treating domestic sewage, types of human health and environmental impacts of the sewer overflow event, and whether the noncompliance was related to wet weather." (m)(3)(i) anticipated bypass notice "at least ten days before the date of the bypass".
status_reason: Federal baseline: reports go to "the Director" (EPA or the state), never to the public. Gives the site the regulator deadline (24 h oral, 5 days written), not a public-notice deadline.
notes: Reports are public records: CWA 308(b) (33 USC 1318(b)) and 40 CFR 122.7(b) ("Claims of confidentiality for the following information will be denied: ... Permit applications, permits, and effluent data").

name: MassDEP CSO API behind the portal (eeaonline.eea.state.ma.us/dep/CSOAPI/api/)
access_detail: Unauthenticated JSON. Endpoints read from the app bundle and called 2026-11-01: GET Incident/GetIncidentsBySearchFields/?[ReporterClass=&EventType=&Municipality=&OutfallId=&WaterBody=&PermiteeClass=&PermiteeName=&VolumeOfDischargeFrom/To=&RainfallDataFrom/To=]&pageNumber=1&pageSize=N&&orderBy=incidentDate%20desc (pageSize 1000 accepted; orderBy submittedDate also works; IncidentFromDate/IncidentToDate returned HTTP 500 in every format tried). GET Incident/GetIncidentById?id={incidentId} (adds compliance self-check answers, parentIncidentId, attachment list, and personal fields reporterName/createdBy/modifiedBy which must be dropped). GET Incident/GetChildIncidentsByParent?id=...&pageNumber=1&pageSize=10& (updates such as 'Ceased'). GET Metadata/GetMetadataForIncident (enumerations: reporterClass, eventType, permiteeClass, municipality list). GET Incident/GetIncidentsForExcel/?{same filters} returns xlsx (26 columns). GET Attachment/GetActiveAttachments?id=... lists the attached advisory (.eml or .pdf); Attachment/Download/{incidentId}/{fileExternalId} returned HTTP 500. GET Permitee/GetPermiteeDetails?permiteeName=... returns the permittee's WWTP outfall with lat/lon only. Requests without Origin/Referer headers returned HTTP 500; with Origin https://eeaonline.eea.state.ma.us and the portal Referer they returned 200.

sample_record.SITE_NOTES: 56" opening in chamber followed by net screening before discharging to the Moshassuck River near the intersection of Moshassuck St and Esten Ave, Pawtucket

cadence: Live alarm feed from NBC's flow/level monitoring (Telog). Page JS has a disabled 60 s refresh; NBC 2022 launch note says overflows show 'as they occur' and stay visible up to 48 hours. On the check date every ACTIVATION_DATE was null (no overflow in the window).
history: None in this endpoint (only the latest activation per site within the window). Archive must be built by polling.
license: none stated
legal_basis: RIPDES permits RI0100315/RI0100072 (2017): NBC must 'develop a system to provide web-based notification to the public on CSO occurrences' (DEM release 2017-10-04).
status_reason: Only real-time, machine-readable, outfall-level sewage discharge feed in Rhode Island; best first build target.
notes: Timezone of ACTIVATION_DATE not stated; map code applies moment.utcOffset('4') before display, so the stored value may be UTC or local - confirm with a live event. 10 of 60 CSO sites carry 'No data available' (no live alarm). name: RSA 485-A:13, I(c) - notice of bypass or upset to downstream water systems
access_detail: Merged chapter page fetched (raw/nh-rsa-485A.html).
legal_basis: RSA 485-A:13, I(c): "Any person responsible for a bypass or upset at a wastewater facility shall give immediate notice of the bypass or upset to all public or privately owned water systems drawing water from the same receiving water and located within 20 miles downstream of the point of discharge. The permittee shall maintain a list of persons, and their telephone numbers, who are to be notified immediately by telephone. In addition, written notification, which shall be postmarked within 3 days of the bypass or upset, shall be sent to such persons." Source note for 485-A:13: 1989, 339:1. 1990, 248:3. 1996, 228:108.
status_reason: Only NH statute requiring notice of a sewage release; it runs to downstream water systems, not the public, and does not cover CSOs as such.
notes: RSA 485-A:2 defines "Bypass" as "the intentional diversion of waste streams from any portion of the wastewater facilities."

name: RSA 485-A:8, II-III - CSO temporary partial use areas; criteria apply during CSO and up to 3 days after
legal_basis: RSA 485-A:8, II: class B waters "shall be considered as being acceptable for fishing, swimming and other recreational purposes ... Where it is demonstrated ... that the class B criteria cannot reasonably be met in certain surface waters at all times as a result of combined sewer overflow events, temporary partial use areas shall be established by rules ..." III: partial-use criteria "shall apply during combined sewer overflow discharges and up to 3 days following cessation of said discharge."
status_reason: Gives NH's statutory 3-day post-CSO window (useful context, not a public-notice rule).

name: Env-Wq 1108.14 Water Quality Standards for Designated Beaches (Env-Wq 1100 Public Bathing Places)
legal_basis: Designated beach "unsafe for public use" if the single-sample standard "is exceeded by 70 counts in any one sample or by any amount in 2 or more samples taken during the same sampling event" or the geometric-mean standard "is exceeded in 3 samples over a 60-day period." Freshwater: E. coli >88 counts/100 mL single, geometric mean 47. Saltwater: Enterococci >104 single, geometric mean 35. On exceedance the owner shall "Retest for bacteria" and "Post a bacteria advisory provided by the department." Cyanobacteria advisory when scum is dominant (>50% of algal cell count) or total cyanobacteria >70,000 cells/mL.
status_reason: Defines when NH beach advisories are issued.

name: 06-096 CMR Chapter 570, Combined Sewer Overflow Abatement (DEP rule)
access_detail: Word .doc from the Secretary of State rules page, linked from the DEP CSO page; converted with textutil (raw/ch570.txt).
cadence: Annual CSO progress report and 'CSO Activity and Volumes' form for the previous calendar year (Ch. 570 s.6-7); permits set the due date as March 1.
legal_basis: 06-096 CMR Ch. 570; authority 38 M.R.S. s.341-D and s.464(2-B). Effective March 14, 1975; repealed and replaced February 5, 2000.
status_reason: Primary legal basis. It requires public notice of CSO impacts, but only as an annual newspaper notice, permanent signs and direct letters; there is no per-event deadline.
notes: Key text, s.3(B)(3)(b): 'a minimum notification program must consist of: (i) Timely annual publication of prominent notices in newspapers having general circulation in the area affected by CSO discharges; (ii) Posting of permanent signs, where feasible, at locations that afford public access to water affected by CSO discharges such as parks and boat launches; and (iii) Direct written contact with persons known to have particular interest in the use of land or waters affected by CSO discharges.' 'All notices must include a description of the area and uses impacted by CSO discharges, the nature, times and conditions of impacts, and precautions that should be observed by the public.' Nine minimum controls s.5(H): 'Public notification to ensure adequate knowledge of CSO occurrences and CSO impacts.' s.6 data: 'precipitation from storm events or snow melt flows that cause CSOs, overflow volumes and overflow events for the period of January 1 to December 31 of each year'.

name: 38 M.R.S. s.464(2-B) CSO subcategories and s.464(3)(C) report on status of licensed discharges
access_detail: Fetched statute page (curl, browser UA).
status_reason: Statutory basis for CSO subcategory notice and the biennial status-of-discharges report; no event notification.
notes: s.464(2-B)(C)(6): 'In a manner prescribed by the board, applicants receiving approval of CSO subcategories shall provide notice to the public in the area affected, describing the limitations on use of the water body.' s.464(3)(C): 'During the first regular session of each Legislature, the commissioner shall submit to the joint standing committee ... a report on the status of licensed discharges.' The annual CSO Status Report itself is not required by statute (it is filed under DEP 'legislative reports' and described as informing permittees and the public). 38 M.R.S. s.466 defines 'Combined sewer overflow'.

name: 38 M.R.S. s.414-D Municipal satellite collection systems: unauthorized discharge reporting
cadence: Oral report to DEP within 24 hours of becoming aware; written report on DEP form within 5 days.
status_reason: Only statutory SSO reporting deadline found; reports go to DEP, not the public.
notes: s.414-D(3)(A): 'An initial report of the unauthorized discharge must be provided orally to the department by the owner or operator of the system within 24 hours of the time the owner or operator becomes aware of the discharge.' (B): 'A written report ... within 5 days ... must contain ... the cause of the discharge, the date and time of the discharge, the location of the discharge, information on any water bodies that may be impacted by the discharge, the number of gallons of wastewater discharged'. No public notice requirement.

cadence: Oral within 24 hours; written within 5 days; to DEP only.
legal_basis: 06-096 CMR Ch. 523; MEPDES Standard Conditions D(1)(f) 'Twenty-four hour reporting' (revised July 1, 2002)
status_reason: Defines when DEP must hear about an SSO or bypass; no public notice.

DEP form instructions add: 'any unanticipated bypass which exceeds any effluent limitation in the permit [including sanitary sewer overflows (SSO's) and dry weather overflows (DWO's) from CSO discharge points]'. name: Charles River Watershed Association Flagging Program (boathouse flags, website, Public Flagging API)
operator: Charles River Watershed Association (site built by Code for Boston)
waters_covered: Lower Charles River Basin, Watertown Dam to New Charles River Dam; 13 boathouses in 4 reaches
access_detail: Fetched: GET https://crwa-flagging.herokuapp.com/api/v1/boathouses (boathouse, latitude, longitude, reach, safe, overridden, reason); /api/v1/model (is_boating_season, model_outputs[reach, predictions[time, prediction, safe]], model_version, time_returned); /api/v1/model_input_data (rain, stream flow, gage height, air temp etc). No auth. Swagger docs linked from /api. Email alerts via CRWA; Twitter @crwaflagging.
cadence: Hourly model predictions in season (May to late October); off season the site shows no flags. Site banner seen today: 'The database has not updated in at least 24 hours.'
history: API returns 24 hourly predictions per reach; older history not exposed
license: API: 'CRWA allows open access to its Public Flagging API' (page wording). Code: MIT license (github.com/codeforboston/flagging).
status_reason: Open JSON API, good for the Charles River water page and a direct partner. Flag rules are public. Caveat: 'reason' still reads 'sewage' or 'cyanobacteria' while 'safe' is true off season, so read 'safe' plus is_boating_season, never 'reason' alone.
notes: Rules quoted: 'If any Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) discharges took place in the past 48 hours in the Lower Basin, red flags will be flown downstream of the CSO discharge point.' Cyanobacteria: red 'for the duration of the bloom'. Flags: 'BLUE FLAGS mean the river is safe for recreation.' 'RED FLAGS mean there are public health risks.' 'Email communications from the CRWA are the official source for status updates.' 2025 Cambridge evaluation found flag programs 'well-supported by their recreational communities'.

license: MIT license
status_reason: Reusable reference for a staleness banner, a season switch, manual override with a reason, and a public API. It is an advisory app, not a discharge-event store.

name: Connecticut River Conservancy 'Is It Clean?' (isitclean.us)
operator: Connecticut River Conservancy (built with The Commons)
waters_covered: 250+ recreation sites on the Connecticut River and tributaries in four states
access_detail: Home and how-it-works pages fetched. Site data are embedded in Webflow CMS HTML; the page POSTs site lists to https://is-it-clean-089e6447542b.herokuapp.com/api/v1/weathers to get the 'likely condition'. No documented API or download. Results also go to EPA Water Quality Exchange (so WQP may carry them).
cadence: Weekly sampling May to October (Wednesday mornings at many sites); 'Results are posted to this site's map within 24 hours after the sample was taken.'
history: Since about 2012 (original 'Is It Clean' database); new site launched 26 Aug 2025
license: none stated beyond site privacy/terms link
status_reason: The bacteria source for the Connecticut River, the project's founding river. Partner first: ask CRC for a feed or a WQX pull, and reuse its 'latest sample' versus 'likely condition' split and recency legend.
notes: Categories: 'clean for swimming', 'clean for boating only', 'not clean for either'. Two layers: 'Latest samples: reflect the most recent water test results.' 'Likely condition: based on recent weather and historical trends.' Recency legend: less than a month / 1-12 months / more than 12 months. Disclaimer: 'While we can't guarantee water safety, we give you the tools to assess the risks yourself.' Tip: 'Avoid contact with the river downstream of a sewage outfall'. 2026 season funded by a $50,000 MassDEP grant.

name: Mystic River Watershed Association daily Boating Advisory (recflag API)
waters_covered: Mystic River at Rt 16, Malden River at Rt 16, Upper Mystic Lake (Shannon Beach)
access_detail: Fetched GET https://myrwa-api.org/api/recflag/predictions/ (no auth): per site {name, site{name, description, latitude, longitude}, current{timestamp, timestamp_local, prob, exceedance, predictors, flags, status{type,label,reason}}, history[7 days]}. Map script https://myrwa-api.org/api/recflag/static/map/build.js. Twitter @SafeMystic.

status.label: Good
status.reason: Low probability of elevated bacteria levels.

license: none stated
status_reason: Small, clean JSON with explicit status types including 'unknown' and a plain-language reason. Ingestible for two Mystic waters; also a good status vocabulary.
notes: Status types: good / advisory / uncertain / unknown (CSS shows recflag-status-good/advisory/uncertain/unknown). Page definitions: Good (boating probably safe), Advisory (E. coli exceedances likely or bloom over state guideline), Uncertain (possible bloom), Not Available ('missing data or a system error'). Model built from 80 samples 2015-2016. CSOs are not a model input. MyRWA: 'In general MyRWA recommends not recreating on the water for 48 hours after heavy rainfall.' No Malden River slug in openboatlaunch.

waters_covered: Mystic River, Alewife Brook, Chelsea Creek

name: WBUR 'Map: Real-time sewage overflows into Mass. rivers and bays'
access_detail: Page and https://api.wbur.org/pages?slug=combined-sewer-overflow-map&source=news fetched. The map is a Flourish embed; no data feed exposed.

license: WBUR copyright
status_reason: The closest earlier attempt at what DirtyWaterWatch plans for Massachusetts: it scraped agency alert emails and web pages into one 48-hour map. It is now broken. Its editor's note reads: 'This tracker appears to be malfunctioning and does not reflect the latest sewage overflow information.'
notes: 'This map is powered through online and/or email public alert systems.' 'WBUR is unable to independently verify the status of each CSO.' 'Use caution near waterways with CSO locations during and up to 48 hours after heavy rainfall.' The lesson is source-health monitoring and a visible stale-data state.

name: Cambridge MA CSO Real-Time, Onsite Notification System Evaluation Report (Kleinfelder, 29 Aug 2025)
access_detail: Downloaded (16 MB, 256 pp) to scratchpad, text extracted; not kept in raw.
license: Copyright 2025 Kleinfelder; client use
legal_basis: 2024 MassDEP/EPA water quality standards variance; 314 CMR 16.00
status_reason: The best US survey of on-site real-time CSO notification. It found only five such systems: DC Water, Lancaster PA and Chelsea MA beacon lights, and the ALCOSAN and CRWA flags. It also covers how the public received them.
notes: Findings: beacon systems drew 'limited to mixed feedback'; flagging systems were 'well-supported by their recreational communities'. Beacon cost about $15,660 each; seven Cambridge sites planned. Cambridge's process: flow-meter alarms, then staff verification, then website/email/sign within 4 hours; notices in 9 languages. Water quality buoys rejected (no bacteria sensing). Lists GLOWanus lanterns.

name: Massachusetts Rivers Alliance Sewage Right to Know campaign
access_detail: Fetched. Campaign history, law summary, town-by-town sign-up list, links to the MassDEP data portal https://eeaonline.eea.state.ma.us/portal/dep/cso-data-portal/
legal_basis: Chapter 322 of the Acts of 2020; 314 CMR 16.00
status_reason: Advocacy context and a likely partner. Its town-by-town sign-up list overlaps the MA state agent's discharger table.
notes: Law as summarised by the campaign: notification 'within 2 hours of discovering the discharge', 'updates every 8 hours while a discharge is occurring', warning signage. The campaign won full notification for 'blended sewage' in the final rules. Page undated (about 2022). Says 187 CSO outfalls and 19 permittees (MassDEP 2023 report says 194 outfalls).

name: Swim Guide (theswimguide.org and app)
operator: Swim Drink Fish Canada (with Waterkeeper Alliance affiliates)
waters_covered: 10,000+ locations; New England listings: MA 529, NH 178, RI 106, CT 77, ME 70, VT none (state listing pages, 2026-11-01)
access_detail: Fetched state pages and a beach page (/beach/3842). A Nuxt app; data appear in the server-rendered window.__NUXT__ payload. No public API documented. An open data standard for feeding results in exists (2017 announcement; copy at github.com/dylanneild/opendata).
cadence: Varies by affiliate. MA text: 'Swim Guide checks for the latest information daily, Monday - Friday during the swimming season.'
license: Legal page: trademarks 'licensed for non-commercial use to other organizations'; no data reuse terms found. 'Swim Guide shares the best information we have at the moment you ask for it.'
status_reason: Partner, not a feed. It is the biggest consumer-facing swim app. Its beach record design (separate result and posted dates, feed source health, thresholds, manual rating) is the closest schema to ours. DirtyWaterWatch could offer discharge events to it through its open data standard.
notes: MA beaches are assigned to 'The Swim Guide - Massachusetts' (Swim Drink Fish staff in Toronto transcribing DPH data), not to a local group. NE affiliates seen: NH Department of Environmental Services, Midcoast Conservancy (ME). Colour rules quoted for Provincetown: Green under 104 enterococci single sample or geomean of 5 under 35; Red above; 'Grey when there is no current or reliable monitoring information available.' Out of season everything shows 'No Data Available'.

Orange 'C-S-O' flags lowered after 48 h without overflow. Conflict: Allegheny County Health Department FAQ says alerts are 'usually canceled 24 to 36 hours after sewer overflows end' and gives a May 1 season start, so two agencies give the same public different rules.

name: Michigan EGLE MiEnviro Portal public CSO/SSO/RTB discharge list (JSON behind the search page)
operator: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy

status_reason: The richest statewide discharge record found in the US: initial versus final status, start and end, quality, volume, receiving water and permit, all in public JSON. The model for our event schema and for any state agency we ask to publish. Candidate feed for national expansion.

name: Federal Great Lakes CSO public notification rule, 40 CFR 122.38 (2018)
access_detail: eCFR redirected to an unblock page; text read on LII.
status_reason: Sets the content of a CSO notice (waterbody, location, public access areas affected, start, continuing or ended, end time, volume within 7 days). Use it as the minimum checklist of fields for our event record. It does not apply to New England.
notes: Initial notice 'As soon as possible, but no later than four (4) hours' after becoming aware; public notice must be electronic; supplemental notice 'Within seven (7) days' with volume and end time; annual notice 'by May 1'; recipients include local public health department and 'Indian Tribes whose waters may be impacted'. Signs must stay 'legible, visible and factually correct.'

name: Surfers Against Sewage Safer Seas and Rivers Service (app and map)
waters_covered: Bathing waters and some river spots in England, Wales; 48 of 89 Scottish bathing waters since Sept 2025
access_detail: sas.org.uk answers 403 to scripted fetches. Facts from SAS Data HQ article (4 June 2026, fetched) and press. No public API found.
status_reason: The most-used sewage alert app. Its key lesson is governance: SAS 'does not set the rules for how individual sewage discharges get turned into bathing water alerts'. Each water company's own model decides, so the same red cross means different things by region.
notes: Display: 'a red cross or a green tick'. Inputs combine pollution risk forecasts, sewage alerts from company EDM feeds, and confirmed incidents. Scotland trigger: discharge 'within 2km' of a bathing site; 'will not confirm whether it is safe to swim'. From June 2026 SAS switched to Southern Water's modelled alerts after years of using its own precautionary rule, giving fewer alerts that SAS says are more accurate but 'not yet good enough'. Persistence window after a spill ends was not confirmed. Users can email their MSP from an alert.

name: SAS Sewage Data HQ (live UK sewage map)

license: Thames layer: 'Licensed under CC BY 4.0'

status_reason: The reference schema for an outfall status record: one row per overflow, an explicit offline state, status start time, latest event start and end, receiving water and last-updated time, under an open licence. Copy it for DirtyWaterWatch's outfall table.
notes: Status values seen: -1 (34 overflows; offline/monitor not reporting, inferred from Top of the Poops 'Offline' column), 0 (538, not discharging), 1 (1, discharging). Thames: 'The data is not validated at the point when it is published because we want to be transparent and alert the public to potential issues as quickly as possible.'

name: Water Industry Act 1991 s.141DA: duty to publish near real-time storm overflow information
access_detail: Fetched.
legal_basis: Water Industry Act 1991 s.141DA (Environment Act 2021 s.81); in force 17 May 2024 for specified purposes and 1 January 2025 otherwise
status_reason: A statute that requires machine-timely publication: that a discharge occurred, where, start time within an hour, end time within an hour, 'in a form which allows the public readily to understand it'. It is a benchmark when comparing New England laws (MA: 2 hours plus 8-hour updates).

name: Southern Water Beachbuoy
access_detail: 403 to WebFetch. Facts from Ford et al. 2025 (abstract fetched) and SAS (June 2026).
status_reason: A warning about modelled impact labels. Since April 2022 releases are split into 'genuine', 'genuine but non-impacting' and 'not genuine'. Researchers found 19% of genuine discharge minutes were labelled non-impacting, often across several tide cycles, and some monitors gave false alarms 100% of the time.

name: SewageMap.co.uk and POOPy (downstream-of-spill map and open-source EDM toolkit)

license: POOPy: GNU GPL 3.0
status_reason: The closest product to a 'modeled reach' layer. It traces river sections downstream of spills in the last 48 hours on a hydrological network. About 80% of users are on phones, 300,000+ visitors in a year, and its embeddable maps are used by news outlets.
notes: The 48-hour downstream method is not documented in the README. The GPL licence matters if code is reused.

FAQ (search): 'When a sensor detects an overflow in progress, the Safeswim system automatically overrides the model results at the associated beach with a temporary black pin for 48 hours.' Manual black pins stay until the issue is resolved.

name: Sewage Overflow Community Right-to-Know Act (federal bill, several Congresses)

notes: S.396: notify the public 'as soon as practicable but not later than 24 hours after the time the owner or operator knows of the overflow'; immediate notice to health authorities when an overflow 'may imminently and substantially endanger human health'; requires 'a feasible methodology, technology, or management program for monitoring sewer overflows'.

name: USGS SIR 2013-5166: validation of beach predictive models against the persistence method
operator: Francy DS et al. 2013. USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2013-5166

status_reason: Of 42 models, 24 gave overall correct responses at least 5% more often than using the previous day's sample; models beat persistence on sensitivity (17 vs 4 models meeting goals). A day-old sample is a weak proxy for today.

name: DEC Sewage Pollution Right to Know page, 'Recent NY-Alert Notifications' view
waters_covered: statewide; receiving water as typed by the notifier
access_detail: Server-rendered Drupal view (class c-view--sewage-notification) inside the SPRTK page; each row = <li class='c-view__row'> with a headline span, <time datetime='UTC ISO'> and the full NY-Alert message text. No JSON:API (/jsonapi 404), no view RSS, no node links per alert. Fetched 2026-11-01: 1 row (Warwick SD#1 UPDATE issued 10-31-2026 20:59). Wayback snapshots (2025-10-14, 2025-10-15, 2026-01-09, 2026-01-19, 2026-04-17, 2026-05-15) show 1-15 rows each, so the view lists a rolling recent window (page text says 'within the last 7 days'; observed counts suggest a shorter window or row cap). Scraping is possible; page is behind a bot check for some clients (Wayback captured 403 pages several times).

Discharge location: 50 State School Rd, Warwick, NY ... Waterbody affected: Tributary of Longhouse creek ... Discharge date and time: 05-30-2025 00:00:00 Discharge duration: unknown Hours  Discharge reason: System Capacity -  Sand filter system not operating correctly ... fields: headline (UPDATE:/ENDED:/none + county, municipality, 'Sewage Discharge', waterbody, public area)
cannot_fill: outfall id (only sometimes in location details, e.g. 'Kelsey CSO', 'Regulator 013A', 'SSO #005')
revision linkage (no shared id between initial, update and ended)
cadence: rows appear when notifiers file in NY-Alert; observed DEC view time equals NY-Alert 'Issued' time within seconds (some notifiers' Issued is 1 h behind during DST). Legal deadline: public within 4 h of discovery.
history: rolling window only; older alerts only via Wayback snapshots or DEC Excel workbooks
license: No licence statement on the page; DEC site 'Website and Usage Policies' apply (not quoted; https://dec.ny.gov/about/website-usage-and-policies). Data caveats on page: 'Data quality is not checked by DEC.'
status_reason: The only public, no-login web surface carrying full SPRTK alert text in near real time; scrape-able but fragile and without ids.

The <time> element matched NY-Alert air time for most notices but ran exactly 1 h late for some (Auburn, Skaneateles, April 2026). The page view is a copy of NY-Alert public messages; notices flagged 'does not reach surface water' are not sent to the public (manual).

name: ECL 17-0826-a, Sewage Pollution Right to Know Act (L.2012 c.368)
access_detail: Fetched nysenate.gov (current version dated 2014-09-22). Legislation API needs a key (401).
status_reason: Statutory deadlines and DEC duty to publish
notes: Quote (1): 'Publicly owned treatment works or the operator of a publicly owned sewer system shall immediately, but in no case later than two hours after discovery, report discharges of untreated or partially treated sewage, including combined sewer overflows, except partially treated sewage discharged directly from a publicly owned treatment works that is in compliance with a department approved plan or permit, to the department and the local health department...' Content (a)-(f): volume and treated state; date and time; expected duration; steps to contain 'except for wet weather combined sewer overflow discharges'; location 'with the maximum level of specificity possible'; reason. (2): 'as soon as possible, but no later than four hours from discovery of the discharge' notify local health department, chief elected official of the municipality and of 'any adjoining municipality that may be affected'; 'The same notification shall also be provided within the same timeframe to the general public ... through appropriate electronic media, including, but not limited to, electronic mail or voice communication as determined by the department.' (3): 'The department, in consultation with the department of health, shall post reported information on its website expeditiously and shall prepare a report on publicly owned treatment works and sewer system discharges annually.' (4): public notification regulations 'shall provide only for public notification of discharges that may present a threat to public health'.

name: 6 NYCRR 750-2.7 Incident reporting and notification requirements (amended eff. 2016-11-09)
access_detail: Fetched from Cornell LII (Justia returned 403). Note: 'Amended New York State Register November 9, 2016/Volume XXXVIII, Issue 45, eff. 11/9/2016'.
status_reason: Operational rules: electronic media, CSO waterbody advisories, daily/termination reports, 5-day written report
notes: (b)(2)(i): 'Immediately, but in no case later than two hours after discovery of the discharge, owners and operators of POTWs and POSSs must report all discharges of untreated or partially treated sewage, including combined sewer overflows, to the department and the local health department...' using 'appropriate electronic media as determined by the department'. (b)(2)(ii)(b): 'As soon as possible, but no later than four hours from discovery of the discharge, owners and operators of POTWs and POSSs must notify the general public...' (b)(2)(iii): 'For combined sewer overflows for which real-time telemetered discharge monitoring and detection does not exist, owners and operators ... must expeditiously issue advisories to the general public ... when, based on actual rainfall data or predictive models, enough rain has fallen that combined sewer overflows may discharge. Advisories may be done on a waterbody basis rather than by individual combined sewer overflow points.' (b)(2)(iv): daily reports 'for each day that the discharge continues' within 24 h of the previous report, termination report allowed; 'POTWs and POSSs are not required to file daily and termination reports for wet weather CSO events.' (d): five-day written report, not required 'for wet weather combined sewer overflows that are in compliance with a department approved plan or permit.' The regulation does not name NY-Alert; DEC designates it ('department approved form of electronic media'). Registration plus timely reports = compliance.

name: Md. Code, Environment § 9-331.1 (sewer overflow and treatment plant bypass reporting and public notification)
waters_covered: all surface and ground waters of the State
access_detail: Statute text page fetched (raw/statute-env-9-331.1.html). Amended by 2019 HB 417, Chapter 310, effective October 1, 2019 (bill page raw/hb0417-2019.html).
status_reason: Primary legal basis: 24-hour report to MDE, 5-day written report, and the 2019 posting duties (site sign in Spanish and English; MDE, MDH and local health department websites; health department social media).
notes: Quote (a)(2): "The report shall be made as soon as practicable but no later than 24 hours after the time that the operator or owner became aware of the event." (b)(2)(i) requires the procedures to require that the notification be posted "1. In Spanish and English at the location of the sewer overflow or treatment plant bypass; 2. On the website of the Department, the Maryland Department of Health, and the appropriate local health department; and 3. On any social media website on which the appropriate local health department regularly posts information". (b)(2)(ii) adds notice "within a reasonable time" to downstream jurisdictions, county governments, impacted State parks, DNR and other land managers. (c)(1) health departments make all public-health determinations. COMAR 26.08.10 (2005) has not been amended to carry the 2019 website duties (its administrative history lists only the 2005 adoption).

name: COMAR 26.08.10 Overflows or Bypasses (reports to MDE and local health department; public notification)
operator: Maryland Department of the Environment (regulation); Division of State Documents (publisher)
access_detail: Full chapter fetched (raw/comar-26.08.10-full.html, text raw/comar-26.08.10.txt). The dsd.maryland.gov/regulations/Pages/26.08.10.xx.aspx URLs now redirect to regs.maryland.gov.
license: Site footer: "This version of the laws and codes on this website is licensed under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license with copyright held by the State of Maryland. This version of the laws and codes on this website will be dedicated to the public domain under the CC0 1.0 license 180 days after publication." and "Please do not scrape. Instead, bulk download".
legal_basis: COMAR 26.08.10.01-.11; effective March 28, 2005 (32:6 Md. R. 636); authority Environment Article §9-331.1
status_reason: Defines overflow, the 24-hour telephone report to MDE and the local health department (.03C), 5-day written report (.05A), the 24-hour public notice for overflows entering shellfish, drinking-water, bathing-beach or public-recreation waters (.08A), the 10,000-gallon notice and posting rule (.08C), the advisory duration (.08D) and the notice content (.08F).
notes: .03C: "Reports required by this chapter shall be made by telephone as soon as practicable to the telephone number or numbers designated by the Department, but not later than 24 hours after the time that the owner or operator becomes aware of the event." .08A: "... the owner or operator shall notify the public as soon as practicable, but not later than 24 hours after the time that the owner or operator becomes aware of the event, about: (1) Any overflow that enters: (a) Shellfish harvesting waters; (b) Waters protected as drinking water sources; (c) Waters used as public bathing beaches where people may swim; or (d) Waters used for public recreation where people may boat, fish, or swim". .08C: "if the overflow's total volume at the time of completed repair as measured or estimated using best professional judgment is 10,000 gallons or more, the owner or operator shall notify the public by: (1) A public service announcement or paid advertising in a daily newspaper, radio station, or television station ... and (2) Posting affected areas" (no separate deadline stated in .08C). .08D: advisory stays "until ... sampling data for the receiving water shows return to normal or prior background levels." .08E: under 10,000 gallons with no .08B factors, notice may be via quarterly/annual reports, water bills or a web site. Exclusion .01B(3)(a): 50 gallons or less to the ground cleaned up within 1 hour. The .03C 'by telephone' wording predates 2019 Ch. 310, which repealed the telephone requirement in statute.

Observed: rowsUpdatedAt 2026-11-02 15:55:53 UTC and every row's :created_at = 2026-11-02T15:55:47Z (full table replaced), newest row an SSO starting 2026-11-01 07:00, so latency about one day after the event. Legal: 24-hour report to MDE, 5-day written report.
history: This table: overflows from February 2023 onward (description says 'February 10th, 2023, onward'; min start_date 2023-01-04). Earlier records 2005-01 to 2023-01 in the frozen dataset md-mde-sewer-overflows-2005-2023.
license: Socrata metadata: license 'Public Domain' (licenseId PUBLIC_DOMAIN); attribution 'Maryland Department of the Environment'.
status_reason: The only statewide, daily, machine-readable event table; covers CSO, SSO, plant bypass and unauthorized discharges with NPDES number and volume. Build against it first.
notes: Quality notes from 2025-2026 rows: (1) `id` is a sort-order number (id 1 = newest) re-issued each reload, and the Socrata system :id is regenerated too (all rows share one :created_at). Dedupe on npdes_no+start_date+start_time+overflow_address. (2) Duplicate rows for one event exist (e.g. 2025-01-24 Jones Falls 4,191,760 gal twice; 2025-07-10 Gwynns Falls 400,225/400,125). (3) lat/long sometimes swapped (2025-02-13 Deepdene Rd lat -76.6342) and overflow_longitude is typed text. (4) receiving_water is free text: 'none', 'storm drain', 'Gwynns Falls is about 500 feet away'; 923 rows null/none/N/A/unknown. (5) discharge_volume can be an early figure that the operator later revises (Baltimore DPW layer shows 17,520 gal where MDE shows 11,000 for 500 W University Pkwy 2026-10-27). (6) False alarms stay in: WSSC's 2026-10-26 Westbard Ave report is stamped NON-REPORTABLE (0 gal) but the MDE row remains. (7) A 2026-10-11 Perryville row repeats cause text naming 'Tropical Storm Isaias' (a 2020 storm), i.e. copied text. (8) 455 rows since 2025-01-01 are 10,000 gal or more. penalty_id present on 558 rows.

Sewage sub-record: /prep/api/prepReportSewages?reportId={id}&expand=prepComponentTypeCode,prepSewageCauses.prepCauseCode,prepSewageImpacts.prepImpactTypeCode,prepSewageRemediations.prepRemediationCode . Also prepReportEvents, prepReportMaterials, prepReportReleaseSubtypes. No login, no key. Response wrapper {offset,limit,count,total,results}. total=117,586 on 2026-11-02; 419 reports with incidentDateTime since 2026-10-01, 111 of them sewageRelated=Y. Newest record created the same day (2026-11-02 13:51). Saved raw/prep/*.json. Status log: /prep/api/prepReportEvents?reportId={id}&expand=prepEventTypeCode&orderBy=eventDate%20desc (e.g. 324738: Call Received 2026-08-04T21:30:30, Under Investigation and Assigned 2026-08-05T10:55:36), which can fill revision_history.

cadence: Live: records appear within minutes of a call-center or online report (records created 2026-11-02 seen the same afternoon). Permittees must call within 24 hours (Va. Code § 62.1-44.5 B; 9VAC25-31-190 L 6-7) and file a written report within 5 days; DEQ staff then update volume, cause and status over days to weeks (Douglas Ave record modified 13 days later).
history: Records from previous systems back to before 2008; current PReP schema since 2019-05-29; fields renamed 2022-09-09 (older rows keep old names).
license: Page text: "If downloaded information will be distributed to other entities, the following statement should be included: 'DEQ is the data source. DEQ does not certify that this data represents a complete record. This data is provided to the citizens of the Commonwealth free of charge and for informational purposes only.'" Terms of Use on the same page: information "SHOULD NOT BE RELIED UPON FOR PERSONAL, MEDICAL, LEGAL OR FINANCIAL DECISIONS"; "By downloading any dataset, you are affirmatively stating that you have read and understood these Terms of Use". https://www.deq.virginia.gov/land-waste/pollution-response/pollution-data-and-reporting
legal_basis: Va. Code § 62.1-44.5 B; 9VAC25-31-190 L 6 and L 7; Va. Code § 62.1-44.19:6 B (DEQ dissemination)
status_reason: The best statewide event feed: live, JSON, filterable by sewage flag and date, with volume, receiving water, cause and NRC/VDEM/SSORS cross-ids. Undocumented internal API, so treat as fragile; the ArcGIS export is the documented fallback.
notes: Data quality: free-text waterbody names ("Gillie Creek", "Gravel Run"), duplicate records for one event (Douglas Ave = 324738 and 324765), permit-number field sometimes holds an MS4 permit (VA0088650 = Norfolk MS4), mediaType sometimes wrong (an SSO coded Petroleum). notes: TIME TRAP: epoch values equal the local wall-clock time plus 5 hours all year (e.g. API 2026-08-04T19:16:57 = export 1785889017000 = 2026-08-05T00:16:57Z), so in summer they are one hour late if read as UTC. Convert by subtracting 5 h and treating the result as America/New_York wall-clock.

name: Va. Code § 62.1-44.5 (prohibition of unpermitted discharges; 24-hour notification)
access_detail: Fetched (raw/vacode-62.1-44.5.html). Subsection B: any person who discharges sewage in violation of subsection A 'shall, upon learning of the discharge, promptly notify, but in no case later than 24 hours the Board, the Director of the Department of Environmental Quality, or the coordinator of emergency services appointed pursuant to § 44-146.19 for the political subdivision reasonably expected to be affected by the discharge. Written notice to the Director of the Department of Environmental Quality shall follow initial notice within the time frame specified by the federal Clean Water Act.' Last amended 2016 (cc. 68, 758).
status_reason: The notice deadline the site can cite: 24 hours, to DEQ or the local emergency coordinator, not to the public.

name: Va. Code § 62.1-44.19:6 (Citizen right-to-know provisions), subsection B
access_detail: Fetched. B: 'The Department of Environmental Quality shall provide to the Virginia Department of Health and local newspapers, television stations, and radio stations, and shall disseminate via official social media accounts and email notification lists, the discharge information reported to the Director of the Department of Environmental Quality pursuant to subsection B of § 62.1-44.5, when the Virginia Department of Health determines that the discharge may be detrimental to the public health or the Department determines that the discharge may impair beneficial uses of state waters.' Added by 2020 cc. 958, 1182 (HB 1205); no deadline is set for DEQ's dissemination. A.2 also requires a 'citizen hot-line'.
status_reason: The only statutory public-notice duty in Virginia; it falls on DEQ, is conditional (VDH or DEQ finding) and has no time limit.
notes: The task brief named §§ 62.1-44.19:3 through :7: § :3 is biosolids land application, :4 definitions, :5 water-quality monitoring and 303(d)/305(b) reporting, :7 impaired-water plans. Only :6 concerns discharge notice.

name: DEQ report HD7 (2021): protocol to decide whether an unpermitted discharge has a de minimis impact
access_detail: WebFetch. Required by 2020 c. 1182. Lists triggers for 'more than de minimis' impact: significant fish kill, VDH shellfish closure, 'Significant non-precipitation-related sewage incident reaching surface waters', HABs, human-contact concern, intake contamination. DEQ preferred the human-based option with existing resources; no gallon threshold; no timeline.
status_reason: Explains why DEQ does not publish every spill: dissemination was scoped to non-de-minimis incidents.

name: 9VAC25-31-190 L and M (VPDES conditions applicable to all permits: reporting, bypass)
access_detail: Fetched. L 6: 'If any unusual or extraordinary discharge including a bypass or upset should occur from a facility and such discharge enters or could be expected to enter state waters, the owner shall promptly notify, in no case later than 24 hours, the department by telephone after the discovery of such discharge... The permittee shall reduce the report to writing and shall submit it to the department within five days of discovery'. L 7 a: noncompliance that may endanger health 'shall be provided orally within 24 hours'; L 7 a (1) lists CSO/SSO/bypass report content (event type, structure type, volumes, impacts, wet weather). L 7 a (2) and L 8 b: electronic submission 'As of the start date in Table 1 of 9VAC25-31-1020'. M 2 a: anticipated bypass notice 'at least 10 days before'.
status_reason: Permit-level deadlines: oral within 24 h, written within 5 days, all to DEQ.

name: NPDES permit DC0021199 (DC Water, Blue Plains and the combined sewer system), EPA Region 3
access_detail: Scanned 60-page PDF (no text layer); OCR'd locally to raw/law/blue-plains-npdes-permit.ocr.txt. Cover: 'Effective Date: August 26,2018 / Expiration Date: August 23,2023' (ECHO lists 08/25/2023, status administratively continued). No reissued permit found.
status_reason: The only binding public-notification rule for DC CSOs.
notes: Part III.B.1.h Public Notification (quoted in report): (i) lights on the Anacostia and Potomac, colour A during a CSO and colour B 'for 24 hours after a CSO has stopped'; (ii) a website with CSO locations, health threats, 'record of CSO events by outfall with number, average duration and volume for the prior three month calendar quarter based on modeled results', the light system, and 'nature and duration of conditions potentially harmful to users of receiving waters during and after a CSO event'; (iii)/(iv) semi-annual pamphlets in bills and at boathouses; (vi) bulletin for callers; (vii) 'Maintain warning signs at all CSOs.' DWOs: 'Each dry weather overflow confirmed by the Permittee shall be reported to DDOE and EPA Region III within 24 hours.' Part II: noncompliance that may endanger health reported orally within 24 hours and in writing within 5 days to EPA and DOEE. Part II Section E: quarterly public accountability summary reports on the website. No clause requires notice to the public of SSOs.

cannot_fill: whether the operator issued the press release
cadence: Edited as DWR enters reports; median report latency 15.7 hours after start (2026 rows). Layer lastEditDate 2026-10-30 00:50 UTC, newest report 2026-10-30, so entry may lag a few days. Legal deadline: verbal report within 24 hours.
history: 2026-01-01 to date in this layer; Sept 2022 to Dec 2025 in https://services2.arcgis.com/kCu40SDxsCGcuUWO/arcgis/rest/services/Sanitary_Sewer_Overflows_September_2022_through_December_2025/FeatureServer/0 (3,208 rows).

legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C; permit conditions (24-hour verbal report, 5-day CS-SSO form)
status_reason: Statewide, machine-readable, event-precision SSO feed with start, end, volume, volume to water, receiving water (with DWR stream index), coordinates and 5-day follow-up fields. Built: pipeline/ingest/nc_dwr_sso.py (571 records on 2026-11-04).
notes: Only SSOs reportable to DWR appear (1,000 gallons or more to ground, or any amount reaching surface water): 516 of 571 rows say reached water. deq_program is "Sanitary Sewer Overflow" for every row although the description says storm-related bypasses are included. Not a press release record: it does not say whether the operator issued the 24-hour press release. Timezone settled 2026-11-04: epoch values are true UTC (Raleigh's 2026-05-12 overflow starts 12:21 UTC, the 8:21 a.m. EDT start Raleigh Water published). The ingester also reads any later Sanitary_Sewer_Overflows_since_Jan_<year> layer it finds.

name: N.C. Gen. Stat. 143-215.1C(b) Publication of Notice of Discharge of Untreated Wastewater
legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b); 24 hours set by S.L. 2013 (S.B. 729), formerly 48 hours
status_reason: The public-notice duty: press release within 24 hours for 1,000 gallons or more reaching surface waters; newspaper notice for 15,000 gallons or more.
notes: (b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred ... The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State." (b)(2): for 15,000 gallons or more "publish a notice of the discharge in a newspaper having general circulation in the county ... and in each county downstream ... significantly affected", captioned "NOTICE OF DISCHARGE OF UNTREATED SEWAGE", within 10 days after the Secretary approves the form. Raw: raw/gs-143-215.1C.html

name: 15A NCAC 18A .3400 Coastal Recreational Waters Monitoring, Evaluation and Notification
operator: NC Marine Fisheries Commission (rules); NC DEQ Division of Marine Fisheries (advisories)
status_reason: The coastal advisory rules: pending and full swimming advisories from bacteria results (.3403), and advisories with signs for waters impacted by a wastewater spill and at storm-water discharges (.3404). No set number of hours after a spill.
notes: .3404(b): "A swimming advisory shall be issued by the Division and at least one sign shall be posted at the public access to swimming waters that have been impacted by a wastewater system failure." Sign: "WARNING! WASTEWATER SPILL. SWIMMING IS NOT ADVISED IN THESE WATERS BECAUSE OF THE INCREASED RISK OF ILLNESS." .3404(c): storm drain and pipe signs (the Precautionary status). .3403(d) sign text: "ATTENTION: SWIMMING IN THIS AREA IS NOT RECOMMENDED. BACTERIA TESTING INDICATES LEVELS OF CONTAMINATION THAT MAY BE HAZARDOUS TO YOUR HEALTH. THIS ADVISORY AFFECTS WATERS WITHIN 200' OF THIS SIGN."
